Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.

The F.I.R. in question was lodged initially under Section 354 I.P.C. alleging therein that the daughter of the informant aged about 13 years was caught by the applicant and he was misbehaving with her.
Subsequently, in the statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim alleged that the rape was committed on her.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant states that in the medical on record, the allegations of rape were not corroborated.
The tentative age of the victim was assessed as 15 years.

It is further argued that Deepak @ Babu vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10293661/
1 the applicant is in custody since 11.11.2023 and the trial has not even started and even the statement of the victim has not yet been recorded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the applicant having criminal history of one case,
may be enlarged on bail.
4.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.

5. Considering the medical on record which does not corroborate the allegations levelled by the victim and the fact that the applicant is in custody since 11.11.2023 having criminal history of one case, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Deepak @ Babu be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.403 of 2023, under Section 376 I.P.C. and Section 5(M)/ 6 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2) 5 of S.C. and S.T. Act, Police Station Imiliya Sultanpur, District Sitapur on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
